prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control; boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Elements: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood): auto start per demand/channel depth; needs permissives (suction level, discharge path, healthy motor, open valves, no trips); lost permissive->alarm/stop; maintenance release after isolations verified at shift turnover. Raw Water Screen Channel: sends Rake Torque Snapshot to Maintenance Planner. Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold): sends Alum Batch Ticket to Laboratory Technician; receives Jar Test Photograph Set from Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow); adjusts only within approved limits; shall hold last operator-approved dose if quality data inconsistent/unavailable. North Filter Gallery (Cobalt): stagger washes on rapid headloss. South Filter Gallery: sends Filter Run Exception Note to Chief Operator; breakthrough->out of production until Chief Operator approves. Backwash Recovery Tank: receives spent washwater; returns only after settling/clarity check. Chlorine Contact Basin and Clearwell Level Controller monitored together. Clearwell Level Controller: low-level interlock blocks pumps; sends Clearwell Diver Entry Permit. High Service Pump Header (Juniper): lead/lag, avoids short cycling and pressure swings; produces Pump Bearing Vibration Clip; first demand indication. North Distribution Pressure Station: separate zone asset. South Distribution Pressure Station: starts lead booster when discharge pressure below start band for delay. SCADA Historian Server (Lantern): time-sync master, audit, data storage. Actors: Chief Operator (classifies upsets, closes them; produces Backwash Solids Manifest after solids quantities verified); Duty Engineer (notified when critical and automatic control cannot hold envelope); Laboratory Technician (sends Sample Chain Slip); Maintenance Planner (Quarry; informed of repeated solids handling problems); Distribution Dispatcher (Falcon; notified when treatment changes affect pressure station reserves; acts on sustained deviations only); Chemical Supplier Driver (sends Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log); Residuals Hauler. Chlorine Residual Alarm: pause maintenance, grab sample, hold production increase; during filtration upset = finished water protection issue. Upsets: advisory (monitor), controlled (operator-directed change), critical (immediate protection). Normal resumes when quality stable, residuals done, alarms cleared, Chief Operator closes. S181: When a distribution station is in automatic operation, local controls are expected to sequence pumps within approved limits and report abnormal starts, failures, or valve positions to the control system.
S182: When a distribution station is in local or manual operation, the Distribution Dispatcher records the reason, the expected duration, and the field contact responsible for the change.
S183: The Clearwell Level Controller is checked before large distribution adjustments so that high service pumping does not create avoidable level instability.
S184: The Chief Operator may direct a conservative pumping posture during unusual demand, main repair activity, or recovery from a treatment upset.
S185: The Duty Engineer reviews persistent low-pressure complaints, repeated station alarms, or mismatches between observed pressure and modeled expectations.
S186: Cobalt shall provide a reliable filter service status indication before the control room treats increased distribution demand as available finished-water capacity.
S187: Sparrow records incoming distribution check samples with the pressure zone, collection point, and time needed for control-room review.
S188: The SCADA Historian Server uses the Sample Chain Slip to associate distribution water-quality entries with the operating period shown in the electronic log.
S189: The Distribution Dispatcher sends the Pressure Zone Handoff Card after verifying current pressure-zone setpoints, active alarms, and open field work.
S190: Shift handoff includes any disabled alarms, temporary operating limits, pending station inspections, and customer complaint trends that may affect dispatch decisions.
S191: If communication to a distribution station is lost, the control room assumes the last confirmed operating mode remains in effect until field verification or telemetry restoration proves otherwise.
S192: Field crews notify the control room before opening or closing major distribution valves so that pressure changes can be distinguished from pump or instrumentation problems.
S193: The Distribution Dispatcher coordinates planned hydrant flushing, valve exercising, and main isolation work with pumping schedules to limit avoidable pressure swings.
S194: When a Chlorine Residual Alarm is active, distribution pressure decisions remain coordinated with water-quality response actions rather than being treated as a purely hydraulic issue.
S195: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench provides analytical status through normal plant reporting channels, and the control room uses that status to interpret pressure-zone complaints involving taste, odor, or disinfectant concerns.
S196: The SCADA Historian Server retains pressure, flow, pump status, and alarm data needed to reconstruct dispatch decisions after an event.
S197: During Storm Intake Mode, the Distribution Dispatcher avoids unnecessary zone changes unless demand, storage, or public-safety conditions require action.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
